question_text: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?

why_it_matters.text: Some rights — like free speech and religion — belong to everyone in the United States. But three specific civic powers belong only to citizens: voting in federal elections, running for federal office, and serving on a jury. These are how citizens shape the government. They're the reason becoming a citizen matters.

fun_fact.text: After a person becomes a U.S. citizen through naturalization, they have nearly all the same rights as someone born here: voting, jury duty, running for Congress, even being a Supreme Court Justice. The Constitution sets aside just one job for natural-born citizens — President of the United States.
